subject: pigeons
one_liner: Global payroll, benefits and worker classification for birds that do not recognise your borders.
brand_voice_notes: Employer-of-record compliance-speak applied without irony to feral birds. The company never acknowledges that pigeons are pigeons; it calls them workers, contractors, headcount, and occasionally 'the population on the structure'. Every sentence sounds like it was cleared by counsel. Numbers are specific and slightly alarming. The tone is the tone of a firm that has already found the liability and is now telling you about it. Nothing winks. The word 'squab' is the culinary term for a young pigeon and nobody at the company has noticed.

hero.h1: Every bird on your roof is an unclassified worker.
hero.sub: Squab is the employer of record for feral and semi-feral avian labour across 41 jurisdictions. We handle classification, cross-border grain settlement and the filings your finance team has been quietly declining to open.

features.title: Ledge Audit
features.blurb: Point any camera at a horizontal surface. Squab counts the population, issues provisional worker IDs, and resolves which jurisdiction each bird is standing in at the moment of observation. The median customer discovers they have been an employer since 2019.

features.title: Grain Settlement
features.blurb: Compensation is remitted in grams of mixed seed at the prevailing daily bread rate, cleared through 41 currencies and delivered to the nearest contracted ledge. Settlement completes in under four minutes. Collection remains the responsibility of the worker.

features.title: Statutory Molt Leave
features.blurb: Molt is a protected absence in 29 of our jurisdictions. Squab accrues the balance automatically, holds the ledge open for the duration, and files the notice before anyone in your organisation has to learn what molting is.

testimonials.quote: We fed them for eleven years and called it goodwill. Squab called it compensation and produced a schedule of arrears going back to the Obama administration.

demo_screen_concept: A payroll-run console for one loft. A roster of twelve named pigeons, each row carrying a leg-band ID chip, a duotone ID portrait, the jurisdiction the bird was last observed standing in, a classification badge (Contractor / Employee / Unclassified / Disputed), a molt-leave balance in days, and a weekly grain figure in grams. Jurisdiction filter chips and a live search across the top; per-row classification toggles that recompute a running employer-liability figure in the console header; a detail drawer that slides in with the bird's observation log and filing history; and a RUN SETTLEMENT control that steps a progress rail through four clearing stages and stamps the run CLEARED.

design_direction.style: Vitreous enamel border-formalities signage, arrivals-hall dark mode. The page is staged as the wayfinding and declaration system of an arrivals hall run by a global employment company that has decided a pigeon is a cross-border contractor and files the roof under 'site of engagement'. A deep bottle-green enamel ground (#0D2B22) runs the whole page with no light mode, no glass, no backdrop blur, no clay volume, no bento lattice, no paper stock, no vellum, no drawing-sheet chrome and no trophy shelving. Nothing on the page casts a shadow, because enamel signs do not. Every surface is a flat panel one step lighter (#123227) carrying a 1px bone keyline inset 6px from its own edge, the way vitreous enamel signage is double-bordered, at a uniform 3px radius with corners kept near-square. Structure is carried by keylines, flat floods and hard rules only. The organising move is the plate: each section is a full-width enamel plate opened by a letterspaced bone caption in the top-left corner and closed by a bone rule, so sections arrive as signs bolted to a wall rather than as cards on a website. The core motif is the leg band: a 999px bone-keylined capsule carrying a short alphanumeric worker ID in mono, used as the list bullet, the feature index, the pricing tier badge, the testimonial portrait frame and the section marker, so every discrete item on the page reads as something that has been ringed and registered. The second motif is the declaration stamp: a rotated hairline oval in customs vermilion with letterspaced caps and a date inside it, dropped at the edge of a plate wherever the company is asserting a legal fact. One enamel bone (#EFE7D2) is the sole carrier: the wordmark, every headline, every keyline, every primary CTA and every leg band, always as a flat flood or hairline with bottle green knocked out of it. One rationed customs vermilion (#D6452F) is quarantined strictly to non-compliance telemetry (unclassified birds, disputed status, overdue filings, arrears figures, the denied line in pricing) and appears nowhere decorative, so the only warm colour on a cold page is always the company telling you that you are already liable. Chivo sets the wordmark and headlines in heavy grotesque at monumental sizes with border-agency confidence, tracking tightened to -0.02em at display sizes and set flush left against the plate keyline. Literata carries plain, faintly statutory body copy at 17px with a 1.62 line-height. Every figure that pretends to be workforce telemetry (worker IDs, jurisdiction codes, grain grams, molt-leave days, arrears totals, tier prices) is set in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures inside recessed green wells one step darker than the plate, so it reads like the register, not marketing. Motion is signage-restrained: plate keylines draw in from the top-left once on reveal, leg bands fill to a bone flood on hover, declaration stamps fade up at their fixed rotation, CTAs invert to a bone flood with green type on hover and depress 1px on press, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No light mode, no glass, no blur, no gradients on type, no clay shadow pairs, no offset sticker shadows, no bento lattice, no drafting hairline grids, no rubrication, no versals, no foil bands, no chenille patches, no roundels, no supergraphic arcs, no split-flap numerals, no HUD corner brackets, no drawing-sheet title blocks, no emoji. Reads like a company that files a live bird under 'engaged worker' and considers your windowsill a place of business.
design_direction.archetype: Global payroll / employer-of-record platform product page staged as an arrivals-hall enamel signage system: a declaration hero with a monumental grotesque claim over a workforce telemetry strip in mono, three numbered feature plates indexed with leg bands, testimonial plates with leg-band-framed ID portraits and worker registration numbers, a three-tier engagement schedule with leg-band tier badges, a closing declaration band, and a handoff to the loft payroll console demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Signage-restrained. Plate keylines draw in from the top-left over 500ms once on reveal, leg bands invert to a bone flood on hover with no lift and no scale, declaration stamps fade up at a fixed rotation, primary CTAs invert to a bone flood and depress 1px on press, roster rows in the demo highlight their left keyline on hover, the settlement rail fills stage by stage, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, everything gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-width enamel plate on the bottle-green ground, bone keyline inset 6px from the plate edge. Top-left corner caption in letterspaced mono ('FORM SQ-1 / DECLARATION OF AVIAN ENGAGEMENT') with the jurisdiction count set opposite it. The h1 sits flush left at a monumental Chivo weight across two lines, with one word carried in a bone flood block. Sub-copy sits at a 62-character measure directly under a bone rule. Beneath that, a single row of four mono telemetry wells (workers classified, jurisdictions, median arrears discovered, settlement time) recessed one step darker than the plate. Primary CTA is a bone-keylined pill that inverts on hover; the demo handoff sits beside it as a bare bone underline link. A single vermilion declaration stamp is dropped at the lower-right of the plate at a fixed 8 degree rotation. No hero image: the direction is typographic signage and a photograph would be a second voice on the sign.

images.rationale: Hero skipped: the direction is vitreous enamel signage and a photograph would be a second voice on the sign. Demo earned three: the console is a worker-ID roster, which is photo-shaped, so birds 1-3 are ID portraits cycled across the twelve roster rows and the detail drawer. Testimonial earned one: bird 4 is the ID photo for Ferdinand Two-Ring, the only registered worker among the three quoted; the two human employers deliberately get a 'no band on file' CSS well instead of a headshot, so the photo itself encodes who is registered. All four passed vision judging on the first attempt: single correct subject, bottle-green ground harmonising with #0D2B22, badge framing, no text artifacts, four visually distinct birds.

Muted desaturated institutional palette, restrained contrast, gentle iridescent sheen on the neck feathers.
